Welcome to the Idols Guide. Here we provide all the key information, tips and tricks to help you understand and maximize this game system.

Idols grant your character bonuses when equipped in the dedicated Idol Container. Unlock all the slots of your Idol Container by completing the related Campaign Quests.

Regardless of what build you decide to play, this guide explains everything you need when it comes to Idols. Use all the presented information while planning a build or gearing up for a stronger character and progression.

## Idols

Idols Guide

There are a total of 20 slots that can be unlocked through the Campaign or by completing Dungeons for the first time.

Idols come in different shapes and sizes that must be accounted for when deciding which ones to use.

The sizes are:

- 1x1 - (i.e. Minor Lagonian Idol)
- 1x2 - (Stout Lagonian Idol)
- 2x1 - (Humble Eterran Idol)
- 1x3 - (i.e. Large Rahyeh Idol)
- 3x1 - (i.e. Grand Majasan Idol)
- 1x4 - (i.e. Huge Arcane Idol)
- 4x1 - (i.e. Ornate Heorot Idol)
- 2x2 - (i.e. Adorned Immortal Idol).

The Idol container filled with different kinds of Idols.

Idols that are 1x1, 2x1, and 1x2 are universal and can be used by any class. The other sizes are class-specific (except for Unique Idols) and can only be worn by the appropriate class. Most Idols are the same rarity and come with one Prefix, one Suffix, and no Implicits. Each Idol base type has a pool of Prefixes and Suffixes it can draw from.

Unique Idols like Throne of Ambition don't follow the typical rules and are instead similar to other Unique items, with the exception of being unable to have Legendary Potential.

## The Idol Grid

Idols Guide

On a new Character, you begin with the basic Idol Grid layout - a 5x5 window, with the center and corner squares blocked. However, this can be changed by placing an Idol Altar into the empty slot above your Grid.

Idol Altars change the layout of your Idol Grid, and introduce new purple squares called Refracted Slots that give different bonuses based on the Idols inside them.

These drop from Omen Windows and come with different Affixes that can impact your Idol Grid in various ways, such as adding increased effectiveness to the Prefixes or Suffixes of equipped Idols.

### Idol Altars

Idol Altars are a type of item that you equip above your Idol Grid to change the layout of the Grid. This introduces Refracted Slots into your Grid that provide bonuses to Idols within them, such as 10-50% Increased Effect of Prefixes or 10-50% Increased Effect of Weaver Enchantment Affixes. ## Idol Enchanting

Idols Guide

Idols can only be Enchanted by completing a Tomb or Cemetery. Upon completion, you are presented with an altar. Interacting with the altar opens an interface where a Class specific Idol can be placed and Enchanted. Alternatively, if you have an Idol that is already Enchanted but you wish to replace it, you can use Memory Amber to reroll it.

Note that Tombs and Cemeteries also drop more powerful versions of non class specific Idols, like the Humble Weaver Idol. They have a distinct look and name to differentiate them from standard Idols. They can't be Enchanted, but are typically upgrades for any build that uses non class specific Idols.

The Woven Enchanter UI with an Idol placed inside.

An Enchanted Idol with Weaver's Touch.

Upon Enchantment, the Idol gains a new affix from a special pool of affixes that can only be obtained through Enchanting. Along with the new affix, it also gains an amount of Weaver's Touch, which is similar to Weaver's Will.

After equipping the Idol, there's a small chance when you kill an enemy that one Weaver's Touch will be consumed to upgrade the Enchanted affix on the Idol. This can either result in an additional tier for that affix, or adding a second Enchanted affix.

Note that you can have a maximum of two Enchanted affixes on an Idol and each affix can have a maximum of seven tiers.

## Omen Idols

Idols Guide
Omen Idols are a special type of Idol that drop from Omens in Omen Window encounters. Omen Idols are 1x3 and 3x1 dimensions, but drop with Affixes, otherwise reserved for larger-sized Class Idols. By default, you can only equip a single Omen Idol. Some Idol Altars come with Affixes that increase your Omen Idol limit.
